hits.name: Matt Pocock
hits.text:
Today's hot take:

Agents are actually really good at strategic programming

It's just they aren't RL'd to actually care about it

"Just do the task at hand, don't do anything else"

So all you need to do is to tell your agent to care about its own codebase.

But the truth is that most people actually don't care that much about the codebase, as long as the code works.

This needs to change. Care about the code, and tell your agent to.

hits.name: Matt Pocock
hits.text:
Starting to realise that to make agents strategic, they really just need a clear goal.

I.e. they can hill climb anything (as long as they have the data), but they need to know where they're going.

Feels like I need to make a /the-ideal-codebase skill that helps you define what that goal should be.

Then you can let your agent choose the direction and just try to endlessly improve.

patterns.name: Small model launch + "Nx cheaper" receipt
patterns.why_it_travels: Everyone running agents feels the bill. One number plus a quick personal test lands on launch day.
examples: bcherny: Haiku 5.5 is a good Haiku, 10x cheaper (~93k)
simonw: pelicans + pricing notes on Haiku 5.5 (~26k)
claudeai: Haiku 5.5 launch (~4.5M)

patterns.name: One prompt, personal app for a tiny real-life moment
signals: I built one out of the data
patterns.why_it_travels: Relatable situation, visible artifact, and a link people can try right away.
examples: bcherny: reading on flights app (~127k)
levelsio: personalized travel site via API + MCP (~23k)
stevelacey: travel blog built from 10 years of data (~29k)

patterns.name: Playable inside the post / everything is being decompiled
patterns.why_it_travels: Zero-install demo that people open on the spot; nostalgia does the rest.
examples: levelsio: Quake III with multiplayer inside a tweet (~132k)
leerob: every game is being decompiled (~170k)
BE4T_37: Halo OpenCE in browser (~371k)

patterns.name: Hot take: agents need a goal and permission to care
patterns.why_it_travels: Contrarian one-liner with a practical fix every builder can try in their config.
examples: mattpocockuk: tell your agent to care about its codebase (~86k)
mattpocockuk: agents need a clear goal (~52k)
trq212: higher abstraction still needs lower levels (~333k)

patterns.name: Scheduled bot that nits your own stuff
signals: markdown skills on a cron job
patterns.why_it_travels: Shows agents doing quiet, useful background work; people ask how to get their own.
examples: clairevo: cringe bot of my dreams (~15k)
zachdavis: Cringe Bot runs 3x a week (~17k)
garrytan: markdown skills on a cron job (~433k)

patterns.name: Skills that make your agent reach for better defaults
patterns.why_it_travels: Small installable upgrade with a clear before/after.
examples: mattpocockuk: Vojta skills (~68k)
vojta_holik: good-css (~76k)

patterns.name: Personal assistant reality check (moms, dots, AI wife)
patterns.why_it_travels: Honest, funny take on what everyday people actually want from agents.
examples: clairevo: moms are the slowest adopters (~33k)
jxnlco: dots told me to book 10 plane tickets (~32k)

outsiders.full_text: We’re releasing a broad range of new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model. (github.com/openai/math)
Meet Mistral Large 4, aka Le Chonk. 1T parameters, natively multimodal, 49B active. Open weights release end of October.
Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5: the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we’ve ever released. On average, it costs around 75% less to run than Claude Haiku 4.5.
Roundup of Day 2/ Approve for me (auto-review) now included; simplified API; meeting notes; Decisions API live for builders.
once ASI is here ... people with money will just move to the nicest places on earth ... probably worth buying real estate there now
Let your app choose the right model, tool, or action in near real-time with Decisions API, now in public beta. Up to 10x faster than GPT-6 Luna.
Quasi-RH?! If a human did this, it would be an instant Fields Medal ... They got a zero free strip!!!!
You can do Fourier transforms in O(N log(N)^0.9999999999999) time.
Quant firms are hiring idea guys, not quants ... software is commoditized, ideas are the moat
Alexandr Wang: a swarm of agents with the right agentic loop and evaluation can accomplish more than a team of 100 engineers.
Five paid API usage tiers become three: Build, Launch, Grow. Grow now at $500 in total payments.
You can basically work with agents to write markdown skills and put it on a cron job and do almost every useful type of knowledge work now
JUST IN: Anthropic study finds AI & robots together are already capable of performing tasks covering 81% of U.S. employment.
The Halo OpenCE Experience™ (decompiled Halo in the browser)
working at a higher level of abstraction has always required understanding the lower level ones, I don't think coding agents changes this
guys... it has happened to me. A huge portion of the work I do lately is just from the terminal via agent + some review.
I'm starting to think mathematics were not beautiful because it "describes the beauty of nature" but rather because human mathematicians only went after beautiful but suboptimal descriptions
Jeff Bezos says AI could make one paycheck enough for a family, because people may work fewer days
Introducing BlitzClean! A free, open-source RAM monitor + disk cleaner for Mac ... ranks AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) by RAM ... Made the video with Opus 5.5 medium
Thinking about all the code I wrote by hand. Wow what a dumbass.
within a few months ... sites hosting *fully playable free WASM versions* of AAA games ... more of a cambrian explosion.
Your coding agent knows :has(), subgrid and anchor positioning. It just rarely reaches for them. I built good-css so it does: 47 modern CSS techniques your agent uses first.
Introducing IdeaLens, a detector of AI ideas! Can you tell if the ideas in a piece of writing are from a human or an AI?
Today we're announcing OpenDocRouter: every model for document parsing under one API ... $0.86 to $48.82 per 1,000 pages.
I spent 10 years traveling and never wrote a travel blog. So I built one out of the data. 51 countries, $64/night overall.
Cringe Bot is a team Grok Bot I created to find small problems with the stuff we build ... runs automatically 3x a week, does its own QA, drops up to 5 findings per run with threaded screenshots.

virals_narrative: Outside the watchlist, the last ~48h is dominated by three things: (1) AI doing real math, with OpenAI releasing hundreds of model-made results (~20M) and mathematicians reacting to a quasi-Riemann result (~1.2M) and a tiny Fourier speedup (~1M); (2) cheaper, faster building blocks, led by Claude Haiku 5.5 at about 75% lower cost (~4.5M), Mistral Large 4 "Le Chonk" with open weights coming (~5.3M), and OpenAI's Decisions API plus simpler API tiers (~1.7M and ~480K); (3) agents becoming the normal way to work, from ThePrimeagen saying most of his work now runs through a terminal agent (~311K) and Garry Tan's markdown skills on a cron job (~433K) to Theo's "all the code I wrote by hand" (~140K), with Thariq's pushback that you still need the lower layers (~333K). Small builder launches that travel share one shape: a free tool with a clear job and a video, like BlitzClean (~147K), good-css skills (~76K) and a Cringe Bot that checks a site 3x a week (~17K). For @bobbyships the best angle today is a one-prompt personal tool or a scheduled checker bot shown with a real finding, posted with a link people can open right inside X.
